intro_decoupe.title: The Cut
intro_decoupe.text:
The shop is nearly empty.

Rain taps softly against the windows.

You finish cutting a piece of meat while the radio crackles in the back of the shop.

Your apprentice watches you work.

**"You could do that with your eyes closed."**

client_etrange.title: The Strange Customer
client_etrange.text:
The bell over the door rings.

An old man walks in slowly.

He sets an antique knife on the counter.

The edge is ruined.
The blade is covered in rust.

But the handle bears a strange symbol.

**"Do you know the Diamond Blade?"**

choices.text: "How much do you want for this knife?"

legende.title: The Legend
legende.text:
The old man smiles faintly.

**"A blade that never loses its edge."**

He takes out an old photograph.

It shows several men standing in front of ruins.

All of them wear the same symbol.

**"My father searched for it his whole life."**

depart.title: Closing Time
depart.text:
The shop is silent.

The photograph rests on the table.

You should probably forget this story.

But your eyes keep drifting back to the symbol.

choices.text: Refuse and get back to work.

fin_vie_normale.title: Ending — An Ordinary Life
fin_vie_normale.text:
The years pass.

The shop keeps running.

Sometimes,
you think back on that blade.

And you wonder whether it ever really existed.

port.title: The Harbor
port.text:
The boat rocks gently.

Crates are stacked all around you.

The captain studies the map.

**"The ruins are past the valley.**
**Nobody goes out there."**

danger_cable.title: First Danger
danger_cable.text:
A cable on the boat snaps loose.

A crate slides toward you.

fin_ecrase.title: Ending — Crushed
fin_ecrase.text:
The crate slams into the railing.

You didn't have time.

The captain watches without a word.

The sea keeps rolling.

jungle.title: The Jungle
jungle.text:
The air is heavy.

Insects nearly drown out the sound of your footsteps.

You come across an old stone marker covered in moss.

The same symbol.

entree_ruines.title: The Entrance
entree_ruines.text:
The ruins finally appear between the trees.

Enormous.

Silent.

A stone door stands partly open.

couloir.title: The Corridor
couloir.narrator:
The floor is paved with cracked slabs.

Some look newer than others.
couloir.text:
Every step echoes.

You feel something beneath your feet.

fin_fleches.title: Ending — Arrows
fin_fleches.text:
A click echoes.

Then a sharp pain tears through your shoulder.

The arrows keep coming until there is only silence.

salle_puits.title: The Well Chamber
salle_puits.text:
An enormous chamber opens before you.

At its center:
a black well too deep to see the bottom of.

An old bridge crosses the room.

pont.title: The Bridge
pont.narrator:
The wood creaks under your feet.

Then a rope gives way.

fin_chute.title: Ending — The Fall
fin_chute.text:
Your fingers slip on the wet wood.

The well swallows you.

Before long, you hear nothing at all.

salle_lames.title: The Blade Chamber
salle_lames.text:
Hundreds of knives cover the walls.

All rusted.

All ruined.

Except for one empty spot at the far end of the room.

In a corner,
behind a collapsed pillar,
you catch sight of something gleaming.

Not the blade.

Gold.

choices.text: Take the gold along with the blade.

fin_piege_declenche.title: Ending — Trap Triggered
fin_piege_declenche.text:
A sharp snap echoes through the entire room.

The blades on the walls begin to move.

You realize too late that some of the knives were never meant to be taken.

mecanisme.title: The Mechanism
mecanisme.text:
A door blocks the final passage.

Three symbols are carved into the stone.

You recognize one of them.

fin_salle_scellee.title: Ending — Sealed Chamber
fin_salle_scellee.text:
A deep rumble runs through the walls.

The door slams shut behind you.

The chamber seals itself.

The torches go out one by one.

salle_finale.title: The Diamond Blade
salle_finale.narrator:
The room is small.

Strangely clean.
salle_finale.text:
At the center,
on a stone pedestal:

the blade.

Even after centuries,
it looks brand new.

Light slides along the edge without revealing a single flaw.

dernier_piege.title: The Last Trap
dernier_piege.narrator:
As you lift the blade,
a rumble runs through the temple.
dernier_piege.text:
Stones fall from the ceiling.

The exit is still visible.

fin_principale.title: Ending — The Butcher
fin_principale.narrator: Some blades are worth more than whatever they cut.
fin_principale.text:
It's raining when you finally return to town.

You set the blade down gently on the shop counter.

Your apprentice freezes.

**"Is this it…?"**

You simply nod.

Behind you, the door opens.

The old man walks in.

He looks at the blade for a long time.

His eyes are different now.
Not cold.
Just old.

**"My father would have wanted to see you do this."**

He leaves without saying anything more.

You pick up a cut of meat.

Then you start carving.

The knife slices through the flesh effortlessly.

Perfect.

fin_englouti.title: Ending — Buried
fin_englouti.text:
The temple collapses.

Blade in one hand,
you search for an exit that no longer exists.

The stones keep falling.

fin_perdu.title: Ending — Lost
fin_perdu.text:
You find the blade.

But never the way out.

All the corridors look the same.

The blade glints in the dark.

fin_cupidite.title: Ending — Greed
fin_cupidite.text:
You try to carry off the room's gold.

The weight slows your escape.

The temple buries you with its treasure.

fin_demi_tour.title: Ending — Turning Back
fin_demi_tour.text:
You abandon the expedition before reaching the ruins.

The boat takes you home.

The jungle stays behind you.

And the blade stays with it.

verif_symbole.title: The Right Symbol
verif_symbole.text:
You press your hand against the symbol.

A click echoes from within the stone.

recherches.title: The Research
recherches.narrator: Some stories you go looking for end up finding you.
recherches.text:
You spend the night searching.

Digitized archives.
Enthusiast forums.
An old colonial-era map book.

The symbol shows up three times.

Always near the same coordinates.
Always tied to the same inscription:

*Indestructible blade. Guarded by those who know how to wait.*

A blurry photo shows the entrance to a temple.

Vegetation has swallowed nearly everything.

But the door is still there.

preparation.title: Preparations
preparation.narrator: You've never really prepared for a trip like this one.
preparation.text:
You spend the morning gathering what you can.

A few butchering tools — the sturdiest ones.
A headlamp.
Clothes for the heat and the rain.

On the map the old man left you,
you finally locate the ruins.

West coast of a volcanic island.
Three days by boat from Marseille.

A region no guidebook ever mentions.

You close the shop for a week.
You leave a note for your apprentice.

*Personal matter. Back soon.*

choices.text: Check the map one last time.

traversee.title: The Crossing
traversee.text:
On the first day, you watch the coast disappear.

On the second day, you study the old man's notes.
They describe the temple's traps.
Symbols to recognize.
Passages to avoid.

On the third day, an island appears on the horizon.

Black.
Covered in vegetation.
No harbor in sight.
No lights.

The captain slows the boat.

**"We'll get as close as we can."**

He points to a small boat at the stern.

**"The rest is up to you."**

choices.text: Ask the captain to turn back.

debarquement.title: Landing
debarquement.text:
The small boat runs aground on a black sand beach.

The ship has already vanished over the horizon.

You are alone.

The island is silent, except for the insects and the wind in the leaves.

Ahead, dense forest begins a few yards from the shore.

According to the map, the ruins lie about four hours' walk inland.

You stow your gear.

The old man's blade is in your bag.

You look at it one last time before stepping into the forest.

choices.text: Check the map before moving on.

campement.title: The Abandoned Camp
campement.narrator: Someone passed through here before you.
campement.text:
You come upon an unexpected clearing.

The remains of a campfire.
Long since cold.

Rusted tin cans.
A notebook whose pages have swollen with damp.

You manage to read a few lines.

*Day 12. The ruins are closer than the map shows.*
*The symbols on the marker match what the old man told me.*
*I don't know if I should keep going.*

And further on, a note added in a hurry:

*The right symbol is not natural. Not the sun. Not an animal.*
*It's the tool. The one a man forged. The one that serves.*

The last entry is several years old.

You don't know what became of him.

But the notebook is here.
He is not.

borne_jungle.title: The Marker
borne_jungle.text:
A few hundred meters farther on,
you find the stone marker again.

The same symbol as on the old man's knife.

It is taller than you imagined.
Nearly two meters high.

Around it, the ground is bare,
as if the plants refuse to grow there.

You place your hand on the stone.

It is slightly warm.

Not from the sun.
There is none under this canopy.

bivouac.title: The Night Before
bivouac.text:
The sun sets quickly.

You decide not to go in at night.

You settle against an outer wall.

The ruins make strange sounds in the dark.
Not animals.
Something more regular.

Like some ancient machinery.
Always in motion.

You eat what's left in your bag.

You think about the shop.
About the apprentice.
About the old man's photograph.

All those people who searched for the blade.

You fall asleep without realizing it.

choices.text: Go in now — you're not tired.

antichambre.title: The Antechamber
antichambre.text:
The first chamber is immense.

The ceiling is so high it vanishes into the darkness.

The walls are covered in bas-reliefs.

Men holding knives.
Hunting scenes.
Ceremonies around a gleaming object.

In the center of the room,
a stone basin still holds water.

The air is cool.
Almost pleasant after the heat of the jungle.

You realize you've been smiling without noticing.

gardien.title: The Guardian
gardien.text:
Before you reach the bridge,
you hear something.

A sound of breathing.

In a corner of the room,
something moves.

A silhouette.

Too tall to be human.
Too regular to be an animal.

It hasn't seen you yet.

Or it's pretending not to.

autel.title: The Altar
autel.text:
At the far end of the room,
just before the final door,
there is a small altar.

Dried offerings.
Bones.
An animal skull.

And an inscription beneath it.

You can't read the language.
But one of the words resembles something in the notebook.

You open it.

*"He who recognizes the blade deserves the blade."*

You put the notebook away.

You look at the door.

Three symbols await you.

choices.text: Read the notebook one more time.

bas_reliefs.title: The Bas-Reliefs
bas_reliefs.narrator: Some images speak without needing words.
bas_reliefs.text:
You step up to the right-hand wall.

The carvings are astonishingly precise.

One scene catches your attention.

A kneeling man.
He reaches his hands toward something.
Above him, three symbols are carved side by side.

The first shows a circle with rays.
*The sun — giving light.*

The second shows a serpent coiled on itself.
*The cycle — always returning to the same point.*

The third is different.

Not a natural object.
Not an animal.

A straight line.
An angle.
A point.

*Something made by human hands.*
*Something that cuts.*

In the carved scene,
the man reaches toward that third symbol.

Not toward the sun.
Not toward the serpent.

Toward that one.

technique_apprenti.title: The Right Touch
technique_apprenti.text:
You adjust the knife in his hand.

**"Not like that. Let the blade do the work."**

He tries again.

Better.

**"The secret is never to force it."**

You pick up your cut of meat again.

Your blade glides cleanly through the flesh.

Your apprentice watches you with an expression that looks a lot like respect.

Or maybe just concentration.

The shop bell rings.

localisation_ruines.title: The Coordinates
localisation_ruines.text:
The old man hesitates.

Then he takes out a small folded slip of paper.

Coordinates scribbled by hand.

**"An island. West coast."**

He sets the paper on the counter.

**"No one has gone there since the eighties."**

He gathers his things slowly.

**"My father went twice. He never found the entrance."**

He looks at you.

**"You, though, would know a perfect blade when you saw one."**

He says it as if it were obvious.

choices.text: Ask why he doesn't search for it himself.

vieillard_part.title: The Old Man Leaves
vieillard_part.text:
The old man picks up his old knife.

He heads for the door.

Then he stops.

He laughs softly.

Not unkindly.
Like someone who has just told a good joke
and is waiting for you to get it.

**"Good luck, butcher."**

The bell rings.

The door closes.

You're left alone with the photograph on the counter.

And something strange in your chest.

Not fear.

Something older than that.

vieil_homme_apparait.title: A Familiar Voice
vieil_homme_apparait.text:
You hold the blade.

It is lighter than you imagined.
Perfectly balanced.

Then you hear something.

Footsteps.

Slow.
Sure.

You turn around.

The old man is there.

He no longer looks old.

He stands straight.
His eyes are cold.
His hands no longer tremble.

**"I knew you'd find the way."**

He smiles.

**"That's why I came to meet you."**

confrontation.title: The Confrontation
confrontation.text:
**"Give me the blade."**

He takes a step toward you.

**"My father searched for it. His father before him."**
**"It belongs to us."**

A rumble runs through the temple.

Stones begin to fall from the ceiling.

You both have the same reflex.

Look up at the ceiling.
Look at the exit.
Look at the blade.

He holds out his hand.

choices.text: Run for the exit with the blade.

fuite_temple.title: The Escape
fuite_temple.text:
You both run.

The temple collapses behind you.

In the corridor, the old man stumbles.

You could keep going.

You stop.

choices.text: Help him back to his feet.

fin_trahison.title: Ending — Betrayal
fin_trahison.text:
You place the blade in his hand.

He doesn't say thank you.

He bolts for the exit.

You watch him disappear down the corridor.

The temple keeps crumbling around you.

You run too.

But the stones fall faster than you.

You don't have the blade.

You have nothing left.
